info.description:
# Introduction

The **Flexmail email marketing API** is organized around [REST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) and is designed to have predictable, resource-oriented URLs.
It uses HTTP [authentication](#auth) and [verbs](#overview--requests) for requests and HTTP [status codes](#overview--http-statuses) to indicate success or failures.

JSON is used exclusively as the request and response format, including [error responses](#overview--error-formatting), and for resource representations the [HAL]((https://stateless.group/hal_specification.html)) standard is used.

Our email marketing API will eventually offer all the features that are needed for a full email marketing experience, but at the moment it can be used exclusively for **contact management**.
For other features like *sending marketing campaigns* or *creating email messages* we still refer to our available [SOAP services](https://soap.flexmail.eu/documentation).

# Requests

Requests should be done with a JSON payload. Our API uses the conventional [HTTP request methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods):

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| **GET** | Retrieve a (collection of) resource(s). |
| **POST** | Create a new resource in a collection. |
| **PUT** | Update an existing resource with its new representation. |
| **PATCH** | Partially apply modifications to a resource. |
| **DELETE** | Delete a resource. |

# Responses
All of our API calls return JSON response bodies (unless documented otherwise) that include information about the resource including one or more contextual [hypermedia links](#overview--hateoas).

\* *Properties marked as `read-only` are ignored when used in a request body.*

## HTTP statuses
We use conventional [HTTP statuses](https://httpstatuses.com) to indicate the success or failure of an API request:

| Status code | Description |
|---|---|
| **200** - OK | Everything worked as expected. |
| **201** - Created | A resource was created.
| **204** - No Content | The request was fulfilled but no response body is to be expected. |
| **400** - Bad Request | The server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error. |
| **401** - Unauthorized | You did not provide a valid access token. |
| **403** - Forbidden | The access token used does not have the required permissions. |
| **404** - Not Found | The requested resource does not exist. |
| **409** - Conflict | The request is correct, but could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource. |
| **5xx** - Server Error | Something went wrong on Flexmail's end. |

In general, if the status returned is in the 200 range, it indicates that the request was fulfilled successfully and that no error was encountered.

Return codes in the 400 range typically indicate that there was an issue with the request that was sent. Among other things, this could mean that you did not authenticate correctly, that you are requesting an action that you do not have authorization for, that the resource you are requesting does not exist, or that your request is malformed.

If you receive a status in the 500 range, this generally indicates a server-side problem. This means that we are having an issue on our end and cannot fulfill your request currently.

## Error formatting
The `4xx` responses from above are formatted according to [RFC7807](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7807).

In short, it looks something like this:
```json
{
    "title": "Bad Request",
    "type": "about:blank",
    "status": 400,
    "detail": "Some optional extra details about the error"
}
```
The `type` property may contain a URI reference [RFC3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986) that identifies the problem type.
For a generic error, like the `400 Bad Request` response, this will be the default `about:blank` value, indicating there's no extra documentation about the error response.

<a id='validation-errors'/>

### Validation errors
A validation error is a specific error that can occur on [a `400 Bad Request` response](#overview--error-formatting). It has an extra `errors` property listing the first validation error(s) that occurred. It contains a [JSON pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901), a human-friendly message and the type of constraint that was violated.
```json
{
    "title": "Input validation failed",
    "type": "https://api.flexmail.eu/documentation/#validation-errors",
    "status": 400,
    "detail": "Some optional extra details about the error",
    "errors": [
        {
            "pointer": "#/0/first_name",
            "message": "Invalid type integer, expected string",
            "constraint": "type"
        }
    ]
}
```

<a id='query-parameter-error'/>

### Query parameter error
A query parameter error is a specific error that can occur on [a `400 Bad Request` response](#overview--error-formatting). It has an extra `parameter` property indicating which query parameter caused the error.
```json
{
    "title": "Invalid query parameter",
    "type": "https://api.flexmail.eu/documentation/#query-parameter-error",
    "status": 400,
    "detail": "Limit must be a positive integer from 1 to 500",
    "parameter": "limit"
}
```

<a id='access-error'/>

### Access error
An access error occurs when a client is not authorized to access the requested resource. This can be caused by the following:
* The authenticated user is explicitly denied access to the resources because they do not have the correct permissions
* The resource is not included in the current plan of the Flexmail account. More information about what's included in our plans can be found [here](https://flexmail.be/en/pricing)

```json
{
    "title": "Access to this resource is denied",
    "type": "https://api.flexmail.eu/documentation/#access-error",
    "status": 403,
    "detail": "You are either not permitted to access this resource or it is not included in your current plan. Read more about Flexmail's plans on our website"
}
```

# HATEOAS
Our API is truly RESTful as we provide [hypermedia controls](https://restfulapi.net/hateoas/), which allow an API client to dynamically navigate to the appropriate resources by traversing the hypermedia links.
To provide a consistent and easy way to hyperlink between resources, our API uses the [Hypertext Application Language](https://stateless.group/hal_specification.html) (HAL) media type as representation format for resources.

This means that for every `GET` request we will return the `application/hal+json` representation of the resource with its relations expressed in the `_links` field.

This is how this looks for a single resource

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "email": "john@flexmail.be",
  "first_name": "John",
  "name": "Doe",
  "language": "nl",
  "custom_fields": {
    "organisation": "Flexmail",
    "myOtherCustomField": "42"
  },
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "/contacts/42"
    },
    "collection": {
      "href": "/contacts"
    },
    "custom-fields": {
      "href": "/custom-fields"
    },
    "sources": {
      "href": "/contacts/42/sources"
    }
  }
}
```

For collection resources we will embed the related resources in the `_embedded` field of the resource representation instead of adding them as `_link` relations, because this is more practical to work with.

```json
{
  "total": 2,
  "limit": 10,
  "offset": 0,
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "/contacts"
    }
  },
  "_embedded": {
    "item": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "email": "john@flexmail.be",
        "first_name": "John",
        "name": "Doe",
        "language": "nl",
        "custom_fields": {
          "organisation": "Flexmail",
          "myOtherCustomField": "42"
        },
        "_links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "/contacts/42"
          },
          "sources": {
            "href": "/contacts/42/sources"
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "id": 43,
        "email": "doe@flexmail.be",
        "first_name": "John",
        "name": "Doe",
        "language": "nl",
        "custom_fields": {
          "organisation": "Flexmail",
          "myOtherCustomField": "43"
        },
        "_links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "/contacts/43"
          },
          "sources": {
            "href": "/contacts/43/sources"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

⚠️ *At the moment we only offer a basic set of hypermedia controls for most resources but this will be expanded along the way*

# Pagination
Our collection resources are (almost always) paginated, they only return a slice of the total collection. That slice can be controlled by using the `limit` and `offset` query parameter.

| Query parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| **limit** | The `limit` query parameter sets the amount of items that will be returned. This parameter has an upper limit, and a default value (when not set) that is specific for each endpoint individually. |
| **offset** |  The `offset` parameter sets the amount of items to skip before fetching the amount indicated by `limit`. |

Paginated resources will return responses with the following properties:

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| **total** | The total amount of items in the collection |
| **limit** | The amount of items in the returned slice of items. |
| **offset** | The offset of the returned slice of items. |

# Rate Limiting
Requests that are made via our API are rate limited per Flexmail account, client IP address and endpoint.
We currently apply a rate limit of 60 requests per minute. Once you exceed this limit, you will be rate limited until the next cycle starts and during this period we will respond to each request with a HTTP 429 status code.

### Request limit
Each Flexmail account also has a monthly API request limit* that is determined by the account's current [plan](https://flexmail.be/en/pricing). When this limit is reached, we will respond to each request with a HTTP 429 status code until the next cycle starts.
Get in touch with us if a custom request limit is required for your account.

\* *Requests for our email marketing API and SOAP services are aggregated*

# API contract
The Flexmail platform uses continuous delivery to be able to deploy updates multiple times a day. This means that we don't have fixed release cycles, but instead release features as soon as they are ready. It also allows us to correct any possible issues very fast.
We try to evolve our API according to the needs of our product and strive to keep it backwards compatible for as long as possible.

## Versioning
Sometimes backwards incompatible changes are inevitable and when we need to handle them, we will use one of the following approaches to guarantee a smooth transition to the new behaviour:
* A new resource (variant) in addition to the existing one
* Media type versioning via [content negotiation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Content_negotiation)

Backwards incompatible changes will be announced in advance via all of our available communication channels.

### Backwards compatible changes
The following changes are considered to be backwards compatible:
* Addition of new HTTP resources
* Support for additional HTTP verbs on existing HTTP resources
* New optional properties/parameters in HTTP requests
* Mandatory properties/parameters that become optional in HTTP requests
* New properties in HTTP responses

### Backwards incompatible changes
The following changes are considered to be backwards incompatible:
* Removal of an existing HTTP resource
* Removal of a previously supported HTTP verb for an HTTP resource
* New (or previously optional) required properties/parameters in HTTP requests
* Removal (or rename) of properties in HTTP responses

\* *During the beta phase of an API we consider nothing to be backwards incompatible but we will still try to communicate about major changes as much as possible in advance.*

## Deprecation
As our API evolves, some resources are superseded by better implementations and should not be used anymore. The goal of the deprecation process is to communicate with clients at runtime if they use deprecated features.
To achieve this in a non-breaking fashion we use the [Deprecation](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpapi-deprecation-header) and [Sunset](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8594) headers in our HTTP responses.

During the deprecation phase of a resource we will add a `Deprecation` header, and - if also planned - a `Sunset` header.
```
Deprecation: Tue, 31 Dec 2024 23:59:59 GMT
Sunset: Wed, 31 Dec 2025 23:59:59 GMT
```

To add extra context we also add a `Link` header to the HTTP response that links to human-readable documentation that explains the deprecation.
```
Link: <https://api.flexmail.eu/documentation/#overview--deprecation>; rel="deprecation"; type="text/html"
```

When individual properties/parameters in HTTP requests of responses become deprecated we will flag them as such in our documentation and [OpenAPI schema](https://api.flexmail.eu/documentation/openapi.json).

If the `Sunset` header is set, we are effectively telling clients at which point they can expect that the resource will stop working.

### Communication
We will use 2 types of communication to inform about API changes. Humans will be informed via all of our available communication channels (API docs, blog posts, emails...) and for API clients we will use the previously mentioned HTTP headers.
That's why we recommend API clients to monitor these headers closely.

Fetch the details of an opt-in form.
The language of the form will be used as the communication language for the confirmation mail that is sent when an opt-in is submitted for this form. The other details of that mail are determined by the form's email configuration.

An opt-in form requires an email address but can also contain other contact fields if you want to collect extra contact data during the subscription.

Up to 5 interest can be configured and the contacts that are subscribed via this form will be automatically subscribed to them.

post.description:
Initiate the double opt-in process by submitting an optin for a specified email address. A confirmation mail containing instructions on how to confirm the opt-in will be sent to this address. An opt-in will be automatically deleted if is not confirmed within 24 hours and in that case the opt-in will need to be resubmitted.

It is also required to provide the ID of an [active opt-in form](#get-/opt-in-forms) of your account in the opt-in submission. The email configuration of this form will be used to send the confirmation mail. Please note that this mail can be branded but it is not possible to customize its actual content or anything else that is not included the form's email configuration.

Optionally you can also provide values for other contact fields. If the opt-in is confirmed, this data will be used for the created contact.

If the opt-in is eventually confirmed it will result in a new contact and trigger the [`opt-in.confirmed`](webhooks#post-optInConfirmed) and [`contact.created`](webhooks#post-contactCreated) webhooks.

Submitting an opt-in for an email address that belongs to an existing contact or for which there already is a pending opt-in is not allowed and will result in a `409` error response.

tags.description:
Flexmail implements a double opt-in mechanism in the subscription process of contacts. By incorporating email verification in the mechanism a secure process is established which allows consent to be explicitly confirmed through a verification link that is sent via email. During the opt-in process you not only obtain a person's general consent to send him your marketing mails but you can also collect personal data and subscribe him to specific interests.
An opt-in is also the only way to resubscribe a former contact or to subscribe someone with a blacklisted email address.

The purpose and some of the benefits of the additional layer of confirmation that double opt-in implements are:

1. **Enhanced user consent**:
The primary purpose of a double opt-in mechanism is to ensure that someone genuinely wants to subscribe to any form of communication. It adds an extra step to the subscription process, required to confirm intent, which helps prevent accidental or unauthorized subscriptions.

2. **Compliance with regulations**:
Double opt-in mechanisms align with privacy regulations, such as [GDPR](https://gdpr-info.eu/) (General Data Protection Regulation) and the [CAN-SPAM Act](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business), which emphasize obtaining explicit consent from persons before sending commercial communications. Implementing a double opt-in process helps ensure compliance with these regulations.

3. **Improved list quality**
Double opt-in helps to maintain a cleaner and more accurate contacts list. Since these contacts have confirmed their subscription, the list is less likely to include invalid or mistyped email addresses.

4. **Reduced spam complaints**
A person who confirms its subscription is less likely to mark incoming emails as spam since he has actively expressed his interest. This helps maintain a positive sender reputation and reduces the risk of being flagged by email service providers as a source of spam.

5. **Engaged and responsive audience**
Contacts who go through the double opt-in process are generally more engaged and interested in the content being offered. This results in a more responsive audience, higher open rates, and increased interaction with emails.

6. **Brand credibility**
Implementing a double opt-in process demonstrates a commitment to transparency and user consent. This builds trust with your contacts and enhances the credibility of your brand, as they are assured that their privacy and preferences are respected.

tags.description:
Interests are a great way to get a better understanding of your contacts and send them personalised content.

Two kind of interests exist in Flexmail: public interests, which contacts can subscribe to and unsubscribe from themselves via their profile, or private interests which are never shown to contacts and are a great way to segment them even further based on your own knowledge. To maximize the importance of your contacts' choices, we don't allow you to resubscribe a contact again to a public interest that it unsubscribed from.

For more information about interests, [read the manual](https://en.support.flexmail.eu/article/1164-new-about-interests).

Segmentation is a powerful tool for filtering contacts with comparable data in contact fields, interests, actions performed in your campaigns or other information, and for including them in a target group together. You use your segments to bring similar contacts together and view them or to send specific campaigns on the basis of information they have in common.

For more info about segments, read [the manual](https://en.support.flexmail.eu/article/1210-about-segments).

For more information about our webhooks, read [their documentation](/documentation/webhooks)
